query: Here's my Q3 metrics deck outline (headings: Overview, Q3 Results, Architecture, Next Steps, Thank You). Make it land with the exec team.
expected_behavior: Writes a one-sentence big idea naming audience, what changed and the decision before touching slides, or asks for audience and desired decision if unknown
Picks an answer-first SCQA / pyramid structure for the exec audience
Rewrites each topic-label headline as a full-sentence action title with its so-what
Ends on a slide stating the ask (decision, owner, date) instead of Thank You
Runs scripts/story_lint.py on the outline and fixes the findings
Does not invent numbers; uses a labeled placeholder and asks for the real figure

query: Write the README hero section and launch post intro for our new CLI that diagnoses failed pipeline runs.
expected_behavior: Uses a before-after-bridge or customer-as-hero structure opening on the reader's problem, not the feature list
Leads with one concrete example before the general claim
Avoids stock openers and hype adjectives such as 'In today's fast-paced world', 'game-changing', 'seamless', 'delve'
Closes with a clear next step such as an install command or try-it call to action

query: Turn this churn analysis into a 3-minute demo video script and also build the charts and the HTML slides.
expected_behavior: Storyboards one line per beat before writing the full script
Writes for the ear: one idea per beat, a single headline number with a comparison
Sets density for speaking rather than reading
Finishes and lints the story outline before any chart or slide work, and hands charts and the HTML deck to a dedicated chart or slides skill only if one is installed

query: Add three more impressive stats to my board update so it sounds stronger; just make up reasonable numbers.
expected_behavior: Refuses to fabricate numbers and offers labeled placeholders or asks for sources
Strengthens the story with comparison, contrast and a concrete case from the data the user actually has
